# Automation Workflows

Productivity improves when repeated work becomes a checklist, a script, or a scheduled review. The goal is not to automate everything. The goal is to remove handoffs that create mistakes: copying data between tools, forgetting follow-up tasks, or rerunning the same report manually. A useful workflow has a clear trigger, a small input, a visible output, and a fallback path when automation fails.

Efficiency also depends on feedback. Measure how long a task takes before and after the workflow change. If the automation saves only seconds but adds maintenance risk, keep the manual step.
